subject.title: bug(compaction): safeguard mode allows sessions to grow to context ceiling — wedge causes "Something went wrong" with no in-channel recovery on Slack;  cost in one session

question: After the truncation defect is fixed, should safeguard remain a near-ceiling emergency mode or become a proactive lower-threshold compaction policy?
rationale: The bug fix is source-backed, but changing safeguard semantics affects context retention, compaction frequency, summary-loss risk, cost, and upgrade expectations; code inspection cannot choose that product tradeoff.

options.title: Keep emergency semantics
options.body: Fix truncation correctness, document safeguard as near-ceiling protection, and recommend default mode when proactive compaction controls are desired.

options.title: Make safeguard proactive
options.body: Lower safeguard's trigger threshold for all users and require explicit compatibility, upgrade, and representative workload proof.

recommendation.title: Keep emergency semantics
recommendation.body: Fix truncation correctness, document safeguard as near-ceiling protection, and recommend default mode when proactive compaction controls are desired.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and co-authored the recent related compaction repair and is the strongest available cross-surface owner for the safeguard semantics decision.
